We stayed at MGallery The Bodrum Hotel for a week, right at the start of the season, checking in the day after the hotel reopened, and overall had a wonderful experience. I would recommend visiting a little later in the summer season if you want more activity outside the hotel, as many beach clubs and restaurants were still closed and the area was still preparing for the busy season. The hotel itself is beautiful, with artwork and a very relaxing atmosphere. Although the AC in our original room wasn’t working, the team handled it very professionally and upgraded us to a junior suite, which we really appreciated. The staff throughout the stay were attentive and welcoming. A special thank you to Esra and Hatice at breakfast, who went above and beyond to accommodate our dietary requirements. They remembered our preferences each morning and made sure all our requests were taken care of, which made the experience feel very personal. The concierge team was also fantastic and incredibly helpful with recommendations and reservations for food, drinks, and golf during our stay. We also really enjoyed the complimentary beer tasting hosted by Yasin Uysal, who was friendly, knowledgeable, and made the experience fun and informative. A lovely final touch was the traditional Turkish gesture when we departed — pouring water behind guests to wish them a safe journey and good fortune until they return. Overall, a truly enjoyable stay and we would happily come back.

The good: - Great welcome - the bracelets were a lovely touch - Clean, spacious rooms - The location and the design of the hotel with all the artwork - Great staff particularly Meryem who really made us feel welcome and took the time to get to know us! - The beach area is lovely The bad: - The noise! All night long we could hear doors slamming, people in corridors, lifts being called. Worst nights of sleep I've had in a long time - The shower drainage needs some work. I couldn't wash my hair without having to turn the shower on and off repeatedly to allow it to drain so as not to flood the bathroom - The music at the beach. 80% of the time it was great but the other 20% of the time it was cranked up so loud, you couldn't have a conversation with the person next to you. Avoid loungers in front of the speakers - Service at the beach is abysmal - it'll take half an hour or so to flag someone down to request a drink

Well what a holiday, the hotel itself was outstandingly clean everywhere from the rooms to the pool area and all this was down to the staff who are hard working, helpful, friendly and willing to help you with anything. The rooms were cleaned every day with towels also changed daily, and the water was replaced daily, the maid was so friendly and always checked to see if all was ok with us. Restaurants you had three to choose from, the main one, one by the pool and a La carte restaurants, we only used the main one and the one by the pool. The staff in both are helpful, friendly and are willing to help you with anything. The pool bar restaurant all the food is cooked fresh so it was always very busy from burgers to sea bass fish fillets. The only problem is if you are looking for a full English breakfast you will be unlucky because they don’t do them, eggs, scrambled, fried and omelettes the rest was your continental type breakfast. Lunch was good but had better, the evening meal was very good with sweets to die for. If you want a full English then go to the back of the Hotel as if going to the beach and turn right walk up about three minutes and on the left is a bar called SALT they do one for about £10. A place everyone should visit is the hotel Patisserie. They have cakes that are very,very,very nice. The place to sit and have a drink of a night is the STAR LIGHT BAR on the 3rd floor. Every night you can sit and watch the brilliant sun set which is stunning. It's open from 18.30 to 1.00am, and ask for your named drinks ( JIM BEAM, GORDON'S GIN SMIRNOFF VODKA ) The pool was clean and tidy. This was down to the gentleman who spent all day mopping around the pool and sunbeds, as well as emptying the rubbish in tubs next to the beds, he deserves a medal for all his hard work every day. Sun beds were plenty full but as normal people would put towels on them, spend about an hour on the beds then go off down to the beach and spend nearly all day down there leaving the towel on the bed by the pool. Then come back for the last hour by the pool?? The hotel is about a fifteen minute walk into Turgutreis along the seafront, the centre has loads of shops and bars. Entertanment, well you could say what entertainment because they had live bands, non very good live bands and two dance groups one from Columbia and One from Brazil, The animation team well that's the best thing I can say about them.

This was our first time to a beach resort in Turkey (have only been to Istanbul before) and certainly won’t be our last. The hotel is fabulous. The art is out of this world, some really amazing pieces. We were upgraded to a suite, being an Accor member, and the room was great. Fabulous sea views. Lovely bathroom amenities. Bottled water provided daily. The only negative was that turndown at night was a bit hit and miss as to whether it happened. Breakfast is a very good spread of food. Lots of fresh fruit and predominantly hot Turkish dishes. Eggs can be cooked on request, although not poached for some reason. Esra was particularly helpful at getting my husband’s eggs cooked to how he likes them. We ate in the restaurant on our first night, following a long day of travel. The food was very nice but the menu, in our opinion, was too bulk standard Mediterranean and not local dishes such as meze or fresh fish dishes. Prices fairly high too. The hotel is in a fabulous location with Yalikavak town on your doorstep, if you are prepared to walk. Turn left out of the hotel and walk down the road a short distance. Take the first right and at the end turn left, walking through the boat yard. You then literally follow the road all the way along the edge of the sea into town. You pass various little bars/restaurants and some small Turkish hotels before reaching the main part, where there are lots of restaurants, then some shops and eventually after a long walk, you’ll get to the Marina. Probably to where the main group of restaurants are, is around 25-30 min flat easy walk. The food in these restaurants is excellent. Fabulous fish and good prices. The Turkish people are extremely friendly and wanting to chat, both in the hotel and in town. We wouldn’t hesitate in recommending the hotel and we absolutely will be returning. I think we’ve found our new holiday destination! Thank you to all of the staff and the GM, who was very approachable and happy to chat.
